clue.text: Scorn Dad-is in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A father is in a spot of bother and gets sneered at for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in trouble', but it stands beside the anagram: 'trouble' turns DADIS into DISDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt, the feeling behind looking down on someone.

clue.text: A large number one's to lose-sack

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
one's read as 'one is', giving I and IS... here simply IS
to miss is to lose, as with a chance or a train

explanation.surface: Someone about to be fired muses on how many workers lose their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack an employee is to fire them from a job.

clue.text: This beast alone is adversely affected

indicators.note: something adversely affected has been knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal suffers from being left on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lion is an eared seal, a marine mammal.

clue.text: About in time for match

indicators.note: in places the word for about inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
re is Latin-derived 'concerning', meaning about

explanation.surface: Someone arrives roughly on schedule for a football fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match correspond, just as people who concur do.

clue.text: City man on the board behind the avant-garde

indicators.note: behind puts the chess piece after the word for the avant-garde

parts.note: the avant-garde is what is new and experimental
a castle (rook) is a chessman on the board

explanation.surface: A city businessman with a board seat trails behind the trendsetters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on the board' suggests a company director; it is a chess piece. NEWCASTLE is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a major city in north-east England.

clue.text: Cold-hearted guys won't stay around long!

definitions.text: Cold-hearted guys won't stay around long!

parts.words: Cold-hearted guys won't stay around long!
parts.note: the heartless men are figures literally made of cold stuff, which melt away when the thaw comes

explanation.surface: A warning about callous men who are bound to leave you.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures built from packed snow are 'guys' made of cold material that melt and vanish.

clue.text: Quite small in a way, but very pleasant

indicators.note: in puts the word for small inside the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Something tiny on a road turns out to be delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sweet is charming and delightful.

clue.text: Crush the guy after more than a quarter-fifty thousand

indicators.note: after places the word for the guy behind the letters for more than and a quarter

parts.note: over means more than, as in over a hundred
W, west, is one of the four quarters of the compass; L is the Roman numeral for fifty
he refers to a male, the guy
W, west, is one of the four quarters of the compass; L is the Roman numeral for fifty
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A man gets crushed after surpassing a quarter and some fifty thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm is to defeat completely, to swamp.

clue.text: Making a cocktail requires skill in short

indicators.note: in places the word for skill inside the word for short

parts.note: mini means short, as in a miniskirt
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Mixing a drink takes expertise, in brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

clue.text: Not extant here now

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something exists neither here nor now.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are simply swapped round: now here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that exists nowhere does not exist at all.

clue.text: A winger responsible for disputes

parts.note: to spar is to argue; a row is a quarrel
to spar is to argue; a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A football wide man is to blame for the arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer; it is a bird. 'disputes' gives both halves: SPAR and ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small bird, and birds fly on wings.

clue.text: A natural oversight

parts.note: oversight read as over-sight: the strip of hair that grows naturally above the eye

explanation.surface: A mistake anyone could make.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairy ridge sits naturally over the organ of sight.

clue.text: Traveller's train vandalism without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the point
vandalism wrecks things, so the letters of train are broken up

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that the train has been vandalised, pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. 'Traveller's' is read as 'traveller is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is one who journeys from place to place.

clue.text: A little mite, English, not coloured

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, a mite

explanation.surface: A small English insect lacks any colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain undyed things are pale, without any hue.

clue.text: Declines to provide kitchen equipment

definitions.meaning: basins with taps for washing up

explanation.surface: Turning down the offer of fitted kitchen units.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to drop lower; basins for washing are fixtures in a kitchen.

clue.text: Showing there's a cover-up?

explanation.surface: A film presentation that hides some scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A film presentation is a screen show, and a protective partition conceals what is behind it.

clue.text: Taste before accepting favoured fruit

parts.note: tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: accepting means the word for before takes in the word for favoured

parts.note: ere is poetic for before
in means favoured or fashionable

explanation.surface: Sampling something before enjoying a preferred fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Possibly turn it on about one to prepare food

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the letter for one
possibly signals the letters could be arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Switching something on in order to cook a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TURN into NUTR; IT and ON follow, and 'about' wraps that run round I, which slips in before ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment, what the body takes in to sustain itself.

clue.text: Checking the French earth in a hole

indicators.note: in places the French word inside the word for a hole

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
terre is French for earth or ground

explanation.surface: A French gardener checks the soil in a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent measure is one that holds back or restrains.

clue.text: Having broken code, drink, which is only proper

definitions.note: a clause for what is fitting; the answer is the noun for that propriety

indicators.note: a broken code is rearranged, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Having cracked a code, a celebratory drink seems only right.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is propriety, behaving in a fitting way.

clue.text: Giving trusted leader cause for treachery

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a reason is a cause or motive

explanation.surface: A trusted chief is handed grounds for betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or ruler.

clue.text: Many love tea &coffee

definitions.note: the & is just 'and' joined to the definition

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
love is zero in tennis, O
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Lots of people like tea and coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine variety of Arabian coffee.

clue.text: More can play the violin

indicators.note: play suggests the letters frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: Several people can play the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: CREMONA is the Italian city famous for violin making, and its name was used for its fine violins.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cremona is a violin made in that Italian city by makers like Stradivari.

clue.text: Rough wind from the South East

parts.note: Auster is the classical name for the south wind

explanation.surface: A harsh gale blowing in from the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means harsh or stern, severe in manner.

clue.text: Material-material used in the Church

indicators.note: used in places the fabric inside the abbreviation for the Church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
rep is a ribbed fabric, a material

explanation.surface: Fabric used for vestments in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed hyphen is a dash: the first 'material' is the definition, the second the wordplay. CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled fabric.

clue.text: Lacking ambition, don't move home so often

explanation.surface: Someone lazy is advised to settle in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiftless person is lazy and without drive; to move house less is to relocate less.

clue.text: Direct cattle

explanation.surface: Guide the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to guide; a bullock raised for beef is a kind of cattle.

clue.text: Heartless seaman out to get fish

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A callous sailor goes out to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish.

clue.text: Tries PE perhaps in the break

indicators.note: perhaps signals another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone attempts gym class during a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or pause.

clue.text: O'er or in rage due to a mineral

indicators.note: rage throws the letters into a frenzy, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poetic rage at some mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is rock from which the metal is extracted.

clue.text: The boss of a German organisation

indicators.note: organisation arranges things, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The head of a firm in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager runs a business or team.

clue.text: Salt-within moderation it rates as essential

indicators.note: within signals letters lying inside the phrase moderation it rates

explanation.surface: Salt is fine in moderation, they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid.
